title: From Syndromes to Computation: A General Framework for Logical Operations in Quantum Error-Correcting Codes
authors: Hunter Nelson, Arshag Danageozian, ChunJun Cao, Sophia E. Economou, Edwin Barnes
abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires error-correcting codes that not only protect quantum information but also support useful logical operations with practical physical realizations. Here we develop a general framework in which the stabilizer syndromes of commuting Pauli rotations directly organize logical-gate design. We derive an exact codespace-preservation condition valid at arbitrary rotation angles, providing a common stabilizer-level description for CSS and non-CSS codes and for both Clifford and non-Clifford operations. A particularly useful equal-syndrome specialization reduces Clifford gate design to stabilizer factorization, yields a general generator weight bound of $\lceil d/2\rceil$ for distance-$d$ codes, and systematically extends to logical rotations higher in the Clifford hierarchy. Applied to bivariate-bicycle (BB) and non-CSS Mirror qLDPC codes, the framework gives explicit low-weight Clifford and controlled-phase gates. Our implementations yield new low-weight gates, including an addressed $T$ gate on the $[[16,4,4]]$ BB code, $T$-type rotations on the $[[64,8,8]]$ BB code, and CCZ-, CS-, and $T$-type operations on the $[[36,6,6]]$ Mirror code. We also develop analytic constructions using Clifford algebra bases, which turn the syndrome constraints into explicit algebraic relations and provide a systematic route to logical addressability. We use this approach to analytically construct addressed CNOT, SWAP, controlled, and CCZ-type gates on recursive hypercube codes. An independent construction on middle quantum Reed--Muller codes yields C${}^r$Z gates that saturate the equal-syndrome weight bound. These results establish stabilizer syndromes as a constructive link between the stabilizer structure of a quantum code, the logical computations it can directly support, and the fault-tolerance properties of their physical realizations.
summary: This paper introduces a general framework that uses stabilizer syndromes to systematically design logical quantum gates in error-correcting codes. It unifies the construction of both Clifford and non-Clifford gates for various code types. The work provides explicit, low-weight gate constructions, establishing a powerful link between a code's mathematical structure and its practical computational capabilities.
main_problem: The paper develops a general, systematic framework to design fault-tolerant logical quantum gates in error-correcting codes.
main_result: It establishes stabilizer syndromes as a constructive link, allowing the derivation of explicit, low-weight logical Clifford and non-Clifford gates for various codes.
method: The framework uses the stabilizer syndromes of commuting Pauli rotations to derive an exact codespace-preservation condition applicable to both CSS and non-CSS codes.
model_or_system: The study focuses on Quantum Error-Correcting Codes (QECCs), including CSS, non-CSS, Bivariate-Bicycle (BB), and Mirror qLDPC codes. The goal is to implement logical operations (gates) while preserving the codespace.
key_observables: Stabilizer syndromes, logical gate types (CNOT, T gate, CCZ-), and the Pauli-rotation partition distance.
important_parameters: Code parameters like distance-$d$ and the derived generator weight bound of $\lceil d/2 \rceil$.
main_assumptions: The framework assumes that logical operations can be systematically derived from the stabilizer structure via Pauli rotations.
figures_summary: The notes mention tables summarizing logical actions found in hypercube catalogs and grouping these actions by family, detailing the complexity of the required circuits.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first defining the general syndrome-stabilizer framework, then specializing it for Clifford gates (reducing to stabilizer factorization), and finally applying this to specific codes (BB, Mirror, hypercube) to yield explicit, low-weight gate constructions.
why_interesting: While focused on abstract codes, the systematic link between stabilizer structure and implementable gates is crucial for designing physical quantum hardware architectures, which often involve engineered local interactions.
